title: factorized expert x depth Mirror coordinate
hypothesis: Factorized expert and depth Mirror coordinates can express a Cartesian family of logical role-depth functions from one shared expert matrix with fewer actual bytes than a per-pair coordinate table, when teacher roles factor across expert and depth; independent pair functions should expose the need for private/table parameters.
physical_object: one shared linear expert matrix W
mirror_coordinate: separate expert code m_e and depth code m_l, applied on disjoint hidden coordinate subspaces
logical_multiplicity: 4 x 4 logical expert-depth functions from separately coded expert and depth axes
teacher: aligned mode uses disjoint Givens views for expert identity and depth; independent mode uses unrelated matrix for each expert-depth pair
controls: expert tying plus static per-depth rank-1 LoRA

development.selection_metric: mean held-out MSE across all methods and both teacher modes

storage.serialization: torch.save state_dict plus deterministic config JSON

success_gate: In all three fresh aligned worlds, factorized Mirror MSE <=1.10x the 16-matrix upper control, <=0.10x hard tying and <=1.10x Cartesian Mirror; actual payload <=0.65x untied and <= Cartesian Mirror payload. Report how independent-pair quality degrades without treating 4x4 combinations as independent capacity.
failure_gate: Factorized Mirror misses two or more aligned fresh quality gates, or static per-depth LoRA / simpler expert tying matches it with equal or fewer bytes. Independent-mode failure alone maps the private-parameter boundary.
boundaries: aligned teacher is an optimistic separability case
no router, tokens, or natural-language evaluation
logical combination count is not independent capacity
